Compress PNG to 20KB

PNG is lossless, so photos saved as PNG are usually far larger than 20KB. This page defaults to JPEG output for that reason.

Compression tool

Target size Target size:
Advanced settings

By default the tool keeps quality reasonable (about 62% or higher) and reduces dimensions to reach small targets; tick “Keep dimensions” to prefer full size at lower quality. Aspect ratio is always preserved and images are never enlarged. PNG is lossless and may not reach a small target; JPEG/WebP are lossy. JPEG replaces transparency with white; WebP and PNG keep it.

Can PNG reach 20KB?

Simple graphics with few colours sometimes can. Photographs almost never can in PNG format. If you choose PNG output the tool encodes it once and reports the real size, even if it is above target.

Transparency

JPEG cannot store transparency; transparent areas become white. Choose WebP or PNG output to keep transparency.

Lossless versus lossy

PNG stores every pixel exactly, with only lossless packing. That makes it excellent for logos, diagrams, screenshots and images with sharp edges, but poor for photographs, where the subtle variation in every pixel prevents efficient packing. A photo saved as PNG may be ten or more times the size of a JPEG of the same picture.

That is why this page defaults to JPEG output. It converts your PNG into a JPEG and then searches for the best quality that fits 20KB.

Keeping PNG output

If you need PNG, select it in Advanced settings. The tool encodes once at the chosen dimensions and reports the real size. If it is above 20KB, you will be told clearly. To help a PNG fit, reduce the maximum width and height, since fewer pixels means fewer bytes, or simplify the image to fewer colours in an editor before uploading.

The tool does not apply colour quantisation, so it will not reduce a PNG's palette for you.

Transparency

JPEG cannot store transparency, so converting a transparent PNG to JPEG fills transparent areas with white. If the picture will be placed on a dark background, that white box may look wrong. WebP keeps transparency and is often smaller than PNG for photographic content, but check that your destination accepts WebP.

Screenshots and documents

Screenshots with text compress well as PNG because large areas are flat, but text edges suffer if you push JPEG too hard. If the document must remain readable, keep the width larger and try a higher target such as the 50KB or 100KB tools instead of forcing 20KB.

A realistic plan for PNG files

First decide if the picture is a photograph or a graphic. For a photograph, use JPEG output on this page. For a graphic, try PNG output with a smaller maximum width. If it is still above target, switch to WebP or JPEG, or accept a larger target using the 50KB or 100KB tools.

Why the tool is honest about PNG

Some tools claim to shrink any PNG to any size. That is not possible without discarding information. If PNG cannot fit, this page shows the real size and explains why, rather than hiding it.

Converting PNG to JPG for forms

Many application forms accept only JPG or JPEG. If your picture or signature is a PNG, converting it is straightforward here: keep JPEG output selected, add the PNG, and download the resulting .jpg file. Because JPEG has no transparency, the background becomes white. Check that the picture still looks right on white, especially for signatures drawn with thin lines.

When PNG is the right choice despite its size

Choose PNG when exact pixels matter: pixel art, diagrams with thin lines, screenshots of code, and graphics that will be edited again. In those cases, accept a larger target such as 100KB or 200KB rather than damaging the image with strong lossy compression just to hit 20KB.

Common questions

Why does PNG output stay large?

PNG compresses without losing data, so detailed images stay big. Use JPEG or WebP for a much smaller file.
